title: tcspecial simulator configuration
description:
What tcssim needs in order to stand in for the payloads of a tcspecial configuration: how fast each one sends, and what it does wrong. Nothing here describes a payload -- the configuration does that, and the two are joined by name.

A setting written with nothing after it is a setting not stated, which is what the editor writes into the form it makes: every payload of the configuration and every setting a payload may state, so that a reader can see what there is to answer.

tcssim.description: What tcssim itself is told. Required: tcssim does not start without it, and a harness cannot wait for a simulator without knowing where to ask.

ready.description: The UDP address, as address:port, at which tcssim answers whether it has made its stand-ins. One no other run uses: a simulator left running holds it, and a second one started on the same address is refused.

thermal_mass.description: The thermal masses the simulated payloads are attached to. A mass cools towards its environment and is warmed by the heaters that are on, so that what the vehicle reads is a consequence of what the vehicle drove: three sensors reading one mass agree, where three sending random bytes never do. A mass nothing is attached to is refused.

environment.description: The temperature around it, in kelvin. A mass starts here, with its heaters off, because a vehicle coming up cold is the case a thermostat exists for.

time_constant.description: How fast it loses the difference between itself and its environment, as a length of time: after one of these it has lost all but 1/e of it.

simulated_payload_groups.description: Settings shared by the payloads that name them.

simulate.description: Whether the payloads that name this group are simulated: true for tcssim to stand in for them, false for the real devices. A payload in a group that states it does not state it too.

type.description: What kind of payload this stands in for: one of the interfaces a payload is reached over, a payload that is a program being the program itself and needing no stand-in. Said here as well as in the configuration so that a simulator file paired with the wrong configuration is caught rather than simulating the wrong thing. Empty is not stated.

protocol.description: Which transport, for a network payload: udp, tcp or unix.

payload_address.description: Where the stand-in answers from, where it has an address of its own to bind.

packet_interval.description: How often it sends, as a length of time -- 1 s, 500 ms -- or the word `continuous` for as fast as the payload can be driven. Nought is no length of time and is refused, being the one value a file arrives at by accident. For a payload that sends on its own: one the configuration gives a trigger is asked instead, at the interval of the payload group it is in, so it states none here and there is nothing for an interval to mean.

segment_interval.description: How often a segment of a packet goes, as a length of time or the word `continuous`; defaults to the packet interval.

drop_percent.description: How often a packet is thrown away.

jitter.description: How late a packet may be, as a length of time, chosen afresh for each one and waited out inside the interval. A length of time and nothing else: leave it out for no jitter.

silent_after.description: How many packets before it stops talking.

close_after.description: How many before it hangs up, where it has a connection to hang up.

ignore_trigger_percent.description: How often it does not answer when it is asked.

reads.description: The thermal mass this payload reports. It sends the mass's temperature in the encoding the `to_kelvin` node its readings go to expects, so the format, the scale and the offset are taken from that node and not stated here.

heats.description: The thermal mass this payload warms while the vehicle drives it on. Such a payload sends nothing -- being driven is the whole of what it is for -- and its packet interval is how often it looks for what the vehicle decided.

rate.description: What a heater adds while it is on, in kelvin a second. With `heats` and refused without it.

simulated_payloads.description: One entry per payload of the configuration. Every data handler needs one, and a name here that no handler has is an error rather than a line with no effect.

simulate.description: Whether this payload is simulated: true for tcssim to stand in for it, false for the real device. Required, from this payload or from its group, and not from both: a payload does not override its group's. Empty is not stated.

group.description: A group whose settings this payload takes for whatever it does not state itself.
